clue.text: On reflection, offender admitting dubious tale is game in court

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one piece takes the other inside it
a reflection shows a thing back to front, so the offender's word is read in reverse

parts.note: a sinner is one who offends, morally

indicators.note: a dubious tale is a doubtful, unreliable one, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A criminal who admits a doubtful story is playing games in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On reflection' turns SINNER into RENNIS, and 'admitting' puts ALTE, from 'dubious' tale, inside it. The court of the surface is a law court; real tennis's court is a walled indoor one.
explanation.definitionFit: Real tennis is the original indoor racket sport, played in an enclosed walled court.

clue.text: Back listener supporting right

indicators.note: in a down clue a supporting piece sits beneath the other one, so it comes second

parts.note: an ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: A sympathetic ear backing the right-wing cause.
explanation.definitionFit: The rear is the back part of anything, so the two nouns are synonyms.

clue.text: Father's up, getting tedious — that's terrible!

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading from bottom to top, so the word is reversed

parts.note: PA is an informal word for father; the 's reads as 'is' in the surface
something palling is becoming dull or wearisome

explanation.surface: An exasperated cry that Dad is out of bed and already becoming a bore.
explanation.definitionFit: Appalling and terrible are synonyms, both meaning shockingly bad.

clue.text: Note about working with carbon drink

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the note goes around the other piece

parts.note: TI is a variant of te, the seventh note of the sol-fa scale
a machine that is on is working
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A note on how fizzy drinks are made with carbon dioxide.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonic water is a carbonated mixer, the drink in gin and tonic.

clue.text: Runs year off without a creche

indicators.note: off means out of order or awry, so the letters are rearranged
without tells us the letters of a are not among those used

explanation.surface: Someone running a year without a creche place for the children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges the letters of RUNS YEAR and 'without a' removes the A from them, leaving NURSERY.
explanation.definitionFit: A creche is a day nursery where young children are looked after.

clue.text: Certain to stop Independent with cover

indicators.note: a stopper goes into an opening, so this piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: IND is a standard abbreviation for Independent, as of a candidate
sure and certain are synonyms

explanation.surface: An insurance pitch: guaranteed to stop independent cover elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Being insured means having insurance cover against loss.

clue.text: Women usually must hide options for eating

indicators.note: the words must hide the answer, which runs within them across the gap

explanation.surface: A claim that women tend to conceal what they choose to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A menu is the list of dishes a diner can choose from.

clue.text: Finish old women's gift

parts.note: an end is a finish
W is the abbreviation for women, as on toilet doors

explanation.surface: Wrapping up an elderly lady's present.
explanation.definitionFit: To endow is to give a person or body money or property, a verb sense of to gift.

clue.text: Play down condition subject to articles abroad

indicators.note: subject to means under, so in this down clue the condition sits below the articles

parts.note: UN is a French indefinite article and DER a German definite article
a state is a condition, as in a state of repair

explanation.surface: A condition that is governed by the rules of foreign articles of agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: To understate something is to make it seem less important than it is, to minimise it.

clue.text: Ears may get loss of pressure from bathroom outlets

indicators.note: loss of means the named letter goes missing from the word

parts.note: plugholes are the drain holes in baths and basins
P is the symbol for pressure in physics

explanation.surface: Popping ears from a drop in pressure, oddly blamed on the bathroom drains.
explanation.walkthrough: LUGHOLE is British slang for the ear, from lug, an old word for ear.
explanation.definitionFit: Lugholes is informal British slang for ears.

clue.text: A writer describing small tree

indicators.note: describing can mean drawing a line around, so the writer's word encloses the other

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument
S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: An author writing about a little tree.
explanation.walkthrough: The word 'small' looks as if it belongs to the definition ('small tree'), but it gives the S inside the pen.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspen is a poplar known for its trembling leaves.

clue.text: Measured depth on centre of area and rang

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another follows it, so the depth measurement comes second
the centre of the four-letter word is its middle two letters

parts.note: to sound water is to measure its depth with a line or sonar

explanation.surface: A survey of the depth in the middle of a region, and a bell ringing out.
explanation.definitionFit: Resounded means echoed or rang out loudly, as a bell does.

clue.text: Caller upset by a line getting signal to proceed

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disordered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A phone caller disturbed by a line, then told to go ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: The all-clear is the signal that danger is past and it is safe to continue.

clue.text: We must board the girl's chopper

indicators.note: to board is to get on or into, so the word goes inside the other

parts.note: her is the possessive meaning the girl's

explanation.surface: Passengers boarding a girl's helicopter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chopper' suggests a helicopter for the boarding picture, but here it is one who chops.
explanation.definitionFit: A hewer is someone who cuts wood or coal with an axe or pick, hence one who chops.

clue.text: Remove traces of educated old boy getting prominence

indicators.note: getting prominence means being put in front, so this piece leads

parts.note: OB is the usual abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
literate means educated, able to read and write

explanation.surface: A well-educated former pupil rising to fame.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate is to wipe out entirely so that nothing remains.

clue.text: Brother — that is cunning, in short

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is
fly is British slang for sharp or cunning

explanation.surface: Summing up a sibling's character in a word: crafty.
explanation.definitionFit: Briefly, like in short, means to put it concisely.

clue.text: One of the last competitors?

parts.note: it sounds like someone trailing at the back, but means one of the few still in for the final round

explanation.walkthrough: 'last' suggests coming last; the question mark warns it means the final stage of a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A competitor who reaches the deciding round of a tournament is among the last left.

clue.text: Pleasure of French fair?

parts.note: de is French for of
fair and light both describe pale colouring, as of hair

explanation.surface: Asking whether the joy of a French fairground is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Delight is great pleasure or joy.

clue.text: Travel around islands in resort to find series of notes

indicators.note: around means the travel word surrounds the other piece

parts.note: to go is to travel

indicators.note: re-sort means to sort again, so these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Island-hopping on a holiday to find a sequence of notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A glissando is a rapid slide through a run of musical notes.

clue.text: Naive young girl suffering ennui, e.g.

indicators.note: suffering means in a bad way, so these letters are disordered

parts.note: the abbreviation for for example, taken as its letters

explanation.surface: A typical sheltered girl bored out of her mind.
explanation.definitionFit: An ingenue is an innocent, unsophisticated young woman, especially as a stage role.

clue.text: Analyse and chop up explosive

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means reading bottom to top, so the word is reversed

parts.note: an axe is a tool for chopping
a mine is an explosive device

explanation.surface: Instructions for studying an explosive and then cutting it up.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine is to inspect or analyse closely.

clue.text: Book help for musician

parts.note: assist and help are synonyms

explanation.surface: Booking some help for a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bassist is a musician who plays the bass guitar or double bass.

clue.text: Damned lucky

definitions.meaning: ... is used ironically as a mild curse, as in that ... dog

explanation.definitionFit: The word works both as a euphemism for cursed and in its literal sense of favoured or fortunate.

clue.text: Sing the praises of former tax cut

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the last letter is removed

parts.note: a toll is a charge or levy

explanation.surface: Applauding the reduction of an old levy.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise enthusiastically.

clue.text: Friendly nation taking part in Eton game

indicators.note: taking part in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A friendly country joining in a public-school match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Friendly' is not an adjective about a nice country: Tonga's islands were named the Friendly Islands by Captain Cook.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is known as the Friendly Islands, Cook's name for the Pacific archipelago.

clue.text: Worried mates will hold your once semi-precious stone

indicators.note: to hold is to contain, so the jumbled letters go around the other piece
worried means agitated, so these letters are shaken up

parts.note: thy is the archaic form of your

explanation.surface: Anxious friends clutching a gemstone that was once yours.
explanation.definitionFit: Amethyst is a purple variety of quartz used as a gem.

clue.text: They regularly exercise right to be over-excited

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of the word is taken

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: People who work out every day become giddy.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyper is informal for hyperactive, wildly excited.

clue.text: Scheme of works with no end

indicators.note: with no end means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a plant is a factory or works

explanation.surface: An endless building programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan is a scheme or design for doing something.

clue.text: People who won't believe a good lad returns and twitches

indicators.note: returns means comes back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a son is a lad
tics are involuntary twitches

explanation.surface: Sceptics watching a nice boy come back with nervous spasms.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnostics hold that God's existence cannot be known, so they withhold belief.

clue.text: Ring about name of punishment

indicators.note: about means around, so the ring encloses the other piece

parts.note: a peal is a ringing of bells

explanation.surface: A call about the name of a sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Penal means relating to punishment, as in penal code.

clue.text: Style and energy required for tribe with no leader

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy

indicators.note: with no leader means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a clan is a tribe or family group

explanation.surface: Leaderless tribes need flair and vigour.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is flair or dash, a stylish verve.

clue.text: Cut left nothing at home after offer

indicators.note: after places the following pieces behind the offer

parts.note: a tender is a formal offer
O looks like zero, nothing
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone who quit with nothing left at home after a bid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut' looks like a verb in the surface but is a noun, a cut of meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderloin is a prime cut of meat from the loin.
